early_childhood_ed.details: The Nashville Tennessean's July 9, 2026 election guide on the TN-4 race explicitly lists among Cortese's council record that 'He has supported legislation to help reduce the costs of child care.' This corroborates his previously documented March 2026 Metro Council co-sponsorship of childcare zoning legislation. Cortese is described as focused on 'representation and affordability' and has campaigned on the idea that 'you can't gerrymander your way out of $5 eggs.' He hosted a living room meet-and-greet in the Glencliff neighborhood of South Nashville on July 12, 2026 as part of his TN-4 campaign outreach. No new federal early childhood education policy positions were articulated beyond the affordability framing.

child_hunger.summary: No explicit SNAP, Summer EBT, or school meal positions found. The Tennessean's July 9 election guide noted that the One Big Beautiful Bill — which Cortese's opponent DesJarlais supported — caused approximately 100,000 Tennesseans to lose SNAP benefits. Cortese has not issued a specific response on food programs in the July 7–13, 2026 window.
child_hunger.details: No direct statements from Cortese on child hunger, SNAP, or school meals were found in the July 7–13, 2026 research window. The Tennessean's July 9 guide noted that DesJarlais supported new SNAP work requirements in the One Big Beautiful Bill, which caused roughly 100,000 Tennesseans to lose food assistance — a likely contrast point for Cortese's campaign but no specific statement was attributed to him in the window.

parental_support.summary: New July 7–13, 2026 finding: The Tennessean confirmed Cortese's vision of 'a world where young couples can afford to start a family, where parents don't have to work 60 hours a week to make ends meet.' He described his TN-4 campaign as focused on affordability and representation. Childcare cost reduction is documented as part of his council record. No specific positions on paid family leave or child tax credit found.
parental_support.details: The July 9, 2026 Tennessean election guide quoted Cortese directly: 'I believe we can build a world where young couples can afford to start a family, where parents don't have to work 60 hours a week to make ends meet, and retirees don't have to go back to work because of rising costs.' He is campaigning on affordability broadly, has criticized DesJarlais for supporting corporations that squeeze the middle class, and has documented support for childcare cost reduction legislation. No specific positions on paid family leave, the child tax credit, or federal childcare programs were articulated in the July 7–13 window beyond the general affordability framing.
